PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run ros-wave-c-117; driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null. No human reviewed or tested this package; no hardware was attached and no ROS graph, Gazebo, MoveIt or live simulator was run.

CARD AND RECON. The card's family:ros/RosDriver shape is used unchanged; the card has no entry_symbols. The pinned clone is a ROS 1 / Gazebo pick-and-place demo: launch/initialize.launch:9-53 starts Gazebo, the UR5 arm controller, MoveIt and the custom nodes, and the only ROS-callable actuation that the clone declares is the array of nine vacuum-gripper on/off std_srvs/Empty services that ur5_gripper.py waits for and calls. The selected device is therefore that vacuum-gripper array (robot.gripper), not the arm. The UR5 arm is moved inside the clone's Python nodes through moveit_commander (ur5_mp.py:62-141); the clone declares no ROS service or action for arm motion, and self.arm.stop() is only a process shutdown callback (ur5_mp.py:150-155). The external arm_controller/FollowJointTrajectory path, the camera image stream (src/ur_description/common.gazebo.xacro:40-71), block spawning, the Gazebo model services and the remaining grasping topics are NOT COVERED. The camera is not claimed as a metadata-only integration; it is outside the selected gripper control surface, and an image capability would require the SDK image artifact path. The channel-3 plugin duplicates the topicName grasping2 (ur5.urdf.xacro:477), so only the first plugin's grasping topic is exposed.

SAFETY. The simulated device is R2 because the demo is a UR5 arm that picks and drops a box; the card floor is R0. Every vacuum-off command is declared safe_state=True, and the server invokes all nine after it latches; /ur5/vacuum_gripper/off is also the explicit estop binding. The Empty service reply is only an acknowledgement, not a measured vacuum, a grasp or a stopped arm. Releasing the vacuum may drop a held object, and it does not stop the arm or cancel a MoveIt execution. The failed-service e-stop path is tested: the receipt is failed with [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the 18 vacuum service endpoints (ur5_gripper.py:20-200), the three observation topics and types (Tracker.msg, blocks_poses.msg, ur5_vision.py:47-48, ur5_mp.py:44-45, blocks_poses_publisher.cpp:113), all 21 facts, the fake and the stop against ur5_gripper.py, ur5_mp.py, initialize.launch, the xacro files and the README at the pin. The e-stop was the first channel's /ur5/vacuum_gripper/off std_srvs/Empty call plus nine safe_state=True vacuum-off actions, but releasing the vacuum drops the payload (a de-energizing request, like a torque-off), the libgazebo_ros_vacuum_gripper plugin that answers it is not in the clone, it does not stop the arm, which keeps following ur5_mp's MoveIt plans, and the shipped ur5_gripper node switches every channel on again when ur5_mp publishes flag2 true on cxy1 (ur5_gripper.py:208-237, ur5_mp.py:203-262), so the SDK reported a completed e-stop that certified nothing; the clone declares no service or action at all. Nine facts were also off their lines or claimed more (launch 9-53 without ur5_gripper on 54, the remap cited to the blank line 34, Tracker.msg 1-11 without flag3, blocks_poses.msg 1-6 without z, the licence on package.xml:15 cited as 16, a trigger range without the flag2 test and gripper8_off, two universal 'no stop service' clauses and a 'so only the first topic' inference) and the README fact was labelled upstream_code. The reviewer removed the e-stop binding and safe_state=True (the off commands stay ordinary commands), rewrote safe_state, the docstring and the off descriptions, corrected those facts and added five (the README's file replacement, the cxy1 subscription, the on_shutdown cleanup, the flag2 publications, the GPL header), and rewrote one gap and added two (driver.py); replaced the three e-stop and safe-state cases with one expecting MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, no upstream call and the latch refusing on and off, plus a check that no action claims the safe state, and labelled two fake-only cases (test_driver.py); updated facts.md; and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED and, at R2, G8 SAFE-028; the seven package cases pass, and collect.py reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED until the orchestrator writes status blocked; the author's notes still describe the vacuum-off e-stop. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Simulated UR5 with nine Gazebo vacuum grippers (ROS 1, MoveIt). No acknowledged stop exists: the vacuum off services release a held box and do not stop the arm, ur5_mp keeps executing MoveIt plans, ur5_gripper.py turns every channel on again on the next flag2, and arm.stop() runs only at node shutdown. The vacuum plugins and the camera exist only after the user copies the clone's xacro files over the installed universal_robot ur_description. Unblocking needs a source-backed stop of the arm and a hold rather than a release for the gripper, or a Gazebo pause from vendored source. ur5_mp.py and ur5_vision.py carry GPL-2.0-or-later headers while package.xml says TODO.
